APT-ENG-0651: The error lies in segment (D) 'if he will minded'. In reported speech following the past reporting verb 'asked', the modal 'will' shifts to 'would' and is followed by the base verb 'mind' (bare infinitive V1): 'if he would mind working late'. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0652: The error lies in part (3) 'were evident from their delayed return'. The subject of the sentence is the nominal 'that'-clause ('That the expedition faced unforeseen challenges...'), which is grammatically singular and takes the singular verb 'was evident', not 'were evident'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0653: The error lies in part (4) 'was not yet collected.'. In formal academic English, 'data' is treated as a plural noun requiring the plural verb 'were not yet collected', or the past perfect passive 'had not yet been collected'. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0654: The error lies in part (2) 'perfectly compliment the colors'. The verb meaning to enhance, balance, or complete something is 'complement'; 'compliment' means an expression of praise or admiration. Correct sentence: 'The new decorative pillows perfectly complement the colors...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0655: The error lies in part (2) 'a blunder mistake'. A 'blunder' inherently means a serious, foolish, or careless mistake; combining it with 'mistake' creates an erroneous pleonasm. APT-ENG-0656: The error lies in part (2) 'are a strong leader'. In a pseudo-cleft construction introduced by 'What we need right now', the copula agrees with the singular predicate complement ('a strong leader'), requiring the singular verb 'is', not 'are'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0657: The error lies in segment (A) 'Pavan returned back home'. The verb 'return' already contains the meaning 'to come/go back'; adding 'back' creates an unnecessary redundancy. Correct sentence: 'Pavan returned home when he completed his assignment abroad.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0658: The error lies in segment (B) 'which you’ll'. The relative pronoun referring to human beings is 'who' or 'whom', not 'which'. Correct sentence: 'My older brother, whom you’ll meet later, is a dentist.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0659: The error lies in segment (C) 'that we wanted'. In the absence of an antecedent noun phrase, the relative pronoun meaning 'the things that' is 'what': 'bought what we wanted', not 'bought that we wanted'. Correct sentence: '...last Sunday and bought what we wanted.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0660: The error lies in segment (C) 'we couldn’t be able to'. The modal 'could' already denotes ability; combining 'couldn't' with 'be able to' is a redundant double expression of ability. Correct sentence: '...we were not able to score high' or 'we couldn't score high'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0661: The error lies in segment (A) 'where had he'. Correct sentence: 'I asked my friend where he had learnt to dance so well.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0662: The error lies in segment (D) 'extremely good'. The verb 'performed' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('well'), not an adjective ('good'). Correct sentence: 'My brother performed extremely well in the class test held yesterday.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0663: The error lies in segment (C) 'along this heavy box?'. The prepositional phrase is unidiomatic; one helps someone 'with' a heavy object ('with this heavy box') or helps 'carry/move' it. Correct sentence: 'Won’t you please come to help me with this heavy box?' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0664: The error lies in segment (A) 'they ran fastly'. In English, 'fast' functions as both an adjective and an adverb; 'fastly' is non-standard. Correct sentence: '...they ran fast to catch it.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0665: The error lies in segment (D) 'confirm me whether you'. The verb 'confirm' is transitive and takes the fact or proposition as its direct object, not an indirect personal object; 'confirm to me' or simply 'confirm whether' should be used. Correct sentence: 'Could you please confirm whether you have received all the items...?' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0666: The error lies in segment (C) 'Investing on real estate'. The verb 'invest' takes the preposition 'in', not 'on' ('Investing in real estate'). Correct sentence: 'Investing in real estate can earn you quick profit...' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0667: The error lies in segment (C) 'to beating'. An infinitive of purpose requires the base form of the verb 'to beat', not the gerund 'to beating'. Correct sentence: 'He will be leaving home at 8 a.m. to beat the office rush hour.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0668: The error lies in part (2) 'are qualified'. The distributive pronoun 'Neither' is singular and takes the singular verb 'is qualified'. Correct sentence: 'Neither of the two candidates is qualified.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0669: The error lies in part (2) 'who has'. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural antecedent 'girls', requiring the plural verb 'have'. Correct sentence: 'She is one of the girls who have won the prize.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0670: The error lies in part (2) 'show began when'. Following the auxiliary 'had', the verb must take its past participle form 'begun', not the simple past 'began'. Correct sentence: 'Hardly had the show begun when the storm started.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0671: The error lies in part (2) 'on to buy'. The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund ('insisted on buying'), not an infinitive. Correct sentence: 'He insisted on buying the tickets.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0672: The error lies in part (2) 'accidents have fallen'. The subject 'The number of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('has fallen'). Correct sentence: 'The number of accidents has fallen this year.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0673: The error lies in part (2) 'than me'. The comparative adjective 'senior' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is senior to me.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0674: The error lies in part (2) 'were rewarded'. When subjects joined by 'and' are each preceded by 'each', the verb is singular ('was rewarded'). Correct sentence: 'Each boy and girl was rewarded.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0675: The error lies in part (2) 'when the passengers'. The correlative pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did the train arrive than the passengers boarded.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0676: The error lies in part (2) 'police has captured'. The collective noun 'police' is plural and takes the plural auxiliary 'have captured'. Correct sentence: 'The police have captured the fugitive.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0677: The error lies in part (1) 'Unless you do not work'. 'Unless' has an inherent negative meaning ('if not'); pairing it with 'do not' creates a double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you work hard, you will not succeed.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0678: The error lies in part (2) 'prefer tea than coffee'. The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'I prefer tea to coffee.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0679: The error lies in part (2) 'Bread and butter are delicious'. When two items joined by 'and' represent a single composite dish, the verb is singular ('is delicious'). Correct sentence: 'Bread and butter is delicious.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0680: The error lies in part (2) 'One of the student'. 'One of the + plural noun' requires 'students'. Correct sentence: 'One of the students is absent.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0681: The error lies in part (1) 'She don't know'. The third-person singular pronoun 'She' takes 'doesn't know', not 'don't know'. Correct sentence: 'She doesn't know the way.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0682: The error lies in segment (A) 'She is quiet a generous woman'. The word 'quiet' means making little or no noise; the intended intensifier modifying the indefinite noun phrase is 'quite' ('quite a generous woman'). Correct sentence: 'She is quite a generous woman to have donated such a large amount...' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0683: The error lies in segment (A) 'went to school'. Following the auxiliary 'did not', the main verb must appear in its base form (bare infinitive V1 'go'), not the past tense 'went'. APT-ENG-0684: The error lies in segment (A) 'who live in Delhi'. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the singular antecedent 'My brother', which requires the singular verb 'lives', not 'live'. Correct sentence: 'My brother, who lives in Delhi, has written me a letter.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0685: The error lies in segment (C) 'No least than'. When comparing a countable quantity of persons or items, the idiom is 'No fewer than' or 'No less than', not 'No least than'. Correct sentence: 'No fewer than fifty participants were present for the singing competition.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0686: The error lies in segment (D) 'Each players'. The distributive determiner 'Each' is followed by a singular countable noun: 'Each player', not 'Each players'. Correct sentence: 'Each player must play according to his full potential...' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0687: The error lies in segment (D) 'yet living'. To indicate the continuation of an ongoing state in an affirmative clause, the adverb 'still' is used ('We are still living in the same house'); 'yet' is used in negative clauses or questions. Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0688: The error lies in segment (A) 'you submitted'. In an interrogative clause with the auxiliary 'didn’t', the verb must take its base form 'submit', not the past form 'submitted'. Correct sentence: 'Why didn’t you submit your project on time?' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0689: The error lies in segment (D) 'the new rules only limiting'. The active participle 'limiting' is used erroneously where the descriptive adjective 'limited' is required ('only limited passengers are allowed' or 'only a limited number of passengers'). Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0690: The error lies in option A 'efficient'. The verb 'worked' must be modified by an adverb of manner ('efficiently'), not an adjective ('efficient'). Correct sentence: 'The team worked extremely efficiently under pressure.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0691: The error lies in segment (C) 'the agitators to back in'. The phrasal verb meaning to retreat or withdraw from a position under threat of force is 'back off' or 'back down', not 'back in'. Correct sentence: 'The police told the agitators to back off, else they would lathi-charge.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0692: Option C correctly rectifies the error. The subject 'All the panel members' is plural and takes the plural auxiliary verb 'have been invited', not 'has been invited'. Correct sentence: 'All the panel members have been invited for the monthly meeting.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0693: The error lies in segment (D) 'and punished'. The first clause has an active linking verb ('He was late'), so the coordinated clause requires an explicit passive auxiliary verb ('and was punished') rather than omitting the auxiliary. Correct sentence: 'He was late for school and was punished.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0694: The error lies in segment (A) 'too much clear to me'. The phrase 'too much' modifies nouns; when modifying an adjective like 'clear', 'much too' or simply 'very' is required: 'much too clear' or 'very clear'. Correct sentence: 'The concept became very clear to me after my tutor showed me the diagram.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0695: The error lies in segment (B) 'an cheap dumping ground'. The adjective 'cheap' begins with a consonant sound (/tʃ/), which requires the indefinite article 'a' rather than 'an'. Correct sentence: 'The sea has become a cheap dumping ground for all kinds of waste products.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0696: The error lies in part (3) 'but also for her innovative ideas'. Parallelism with the correlative conjunction 'not only... but also' requires balancing direct objects: 'appreciated not only her dedication but also her innovative ideas', omitting the preposition 'for'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0697: The error lies in part (3) 'where will scientists conduct'. Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0698: The error lies in part (1) 'Were she to have known about the danger'. The inverted past unreal conditional is expressed as 'Had she known about the danger' or 'Were she to know', not the hybrid 'Were she to have known'. Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0699: The error lies in segment (C) 'on the earliest'. The idiomatic prepositional phrase meaning at the first possible opportunity is 'at the earliest', not 'on the earliest'. Correct sentence: 'They ordered the whole area to be disinfected at the earliest.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0700: The error lies in segment (D) 'has prepare well'. The present perfect tense requires the auxiliary 'has' followed by the past participle (V3) form 'prepared', not the base form 'prepare'. Correct sentence: '...because our team has prepared well.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0701: The error lies in segment (C) 'Shamim have not'. The subject 'Shamim' is third-person singular and takes the singular auxiliary verb 'has not', not 'have not'. Correct sentence: 'Shamim has not attended school for four days now.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0702: The error lies in segment (C) 'to her boss until she realises'. The sentence narrates events in the past ('had been writing', 'was not interested'), requiring the simple past tense 'realised' rather than the present tense 'realises'. Correct sentence: 'Alka had been writing to her boss until she realised that he was not interested in resolving her issues.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0703: The error lies in segment (C) 'He doesn’t travel such more'. The modifier of extent in a negative verb construction should be 'much' or 'so much', not 'such more'. APT-ENG-0704: The error lies in part (C) 'where he study Grammar and Latin.'. Correct sentence: '...where he studied Grammar and Latin.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0705: The error lies in segment (B) 'from 3:30 p.m. and 5:30 p.m.'. Correct sentence: 'The sports day events will be conducted from 3:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. on Saturday.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0706: The error lies in segment (D) 'a most luminous'. In superlative comparison across a complete class ('of all city-states'), the definite article 'the' is required: 'the most luminous'. Correct sentence: 'Athens was the most luminous of all city-states of ancient Greece.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0707: The error lies in segment (B) 'ate that lobster'. Following the past perfect auxiliary 'had', the verb must appear in its past participle form 'eaten' (V3), not the simple past 'ate'. Correct sentence: 'After he had eaten that lobster, he began to feel sick.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0708: The error lies in segment (D) 'doesn’t grows on trees'. Following the auxiliary 'doesn't', the main verb must appear in its base form 'grow', not the third-person inflected form 'grows'. Correct sentence: '...that money doesn’t grow on trees.' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0709: The error lies in segment (B) 'is invisible from'. The adjective 'invisible' collocates with the preposition 'to' ('invisible to the naked eye'), not 'from'. Correct sentence: 'There is a whole world out there that is invisible to the naked eye.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0710: The error lies in segment (B) 'be hurry,'. The modal 'must' is followed directly by the base verb 'hurry' ('You must hurry') or the adjective idiom 'be in a hurry'; 'be hurry' is ungrammatical. Correct sentence: 'You must hurry, otherwise you will miss the train.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0711: The error lies in segment (B) 'I was be groomed'. The passive past continuous construction is 'was being groomed', or simple past passive 'was groomed'; 'was be groomed' is ungrammatical. Correct sentence: 'I felt that I was being groomed for success in the world.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0712: The error lies in segment (C) 'will take a seat and'. In indirect speech following a past reporting verb ('asked'), the modal auxiliary 'will' shifts to 'would'. Correct sentence: 'The receptionist asked if Diya would take a seat and wait for the boss to call her in.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0713: There is no grammatical error in this sentence. 'It turns out that my father isn't alone' is grammatically correct and idiomatic. Hence, option A ('No error') is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0714: The error lies in segment (D) 'She is quiet a generous woman'. The word 'quiet' (silent) is confused with the intensifying adverb of degree 'quite' ('quite a generous woman'). Correct sentence: 'She is quite a generous woman to have donated such a large amount...' Hence, option D is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0715: The error lies in segment (C) 'his friends, were'. Correct sentence: 'The boy, as well as his friends, was absent from the class when the teacher came.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0716: The error lies in segment (C) 'by three years'. A duration or period of time ('three years') in the present perfect takes the preposition 'for', not 'by'. Correct sentence: 'She has not written a single novel for three years.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0717: The error lies in segment (A) 'and straightly'. The word 'straight' serves as both an adjective and an adverb in standard English; 'straightly' is non-standard. Correct sentence: 'He does not know how to draw quickly and straight.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0718: The error lies in part (2) 'were present'. The distributive pronoun 'Neither' is singular in formal grammar and takes the singular verb 'was present'. Correct sentence: 'Neither of them was present.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0719: The error lies in part (2) 'who has'. The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural antecedent 'doctors', requiring the plural verb 'have'. Correct sentence: 'She is one of the doctors who have treated this condition.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0720: The error lies in part (2) 'bell rang when'. Following the auxiliary 'had', the verb must take its past participle form 'rung', not the simple past 'rang'. Correct sentence: 'Hardly had the bell rung when the students dispersed.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0721: The error lies in part (2) 'on to come'. The verb 'insist' takes the preposition 'on' followed by a gerund ('insisted on coming'), not an infinitive. Correct sentence: 'He insisted on coming with us.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0722: The error lies in part (2) 'are rising'. 'The number of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('is rising'). Correct sentence: 'The number of candidates is rising steadily.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0723: The error lies in part (2) 'than him'. Comparative adjectives ending in '-ior' take the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'She is senior to him in service.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0724: The error lies in part (2) 'were given'. When subjects joined by 'and' are preceded by 'each', the verb is singular ('was given'). Correct sentence: 'Each boy and girl was given an award.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0725: The error lies in part (2) 'when the whistle blew'. The correlative pair with 'No sooner' is 'than', not 'when'. Correct sentence: 'No sooner did he leave than the whistle blew.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0726: The error lies in part (2) 'police has found'. The collective noun 'police' is plural and takes the plural auxiliary 'have found'. Correct sentence: 'The police have found the missing car.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0727: The error lies in part (1) 'Unless you do not listen'. 'Unless' already means 'if not'; pairing it with 'do not' creates an erroneous double negative. Correct sentence: 'Unless you listen carefully, you will miss important instructions.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0728: The error lies in part (2) 'prefer tea than coffee'. The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'than'. Correct sentence: 'I prefer tea to coffee.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0729: The error lies in part (2) 'are his favourite'. When two nouns joined by 'and' represent a single composite dish, the verb is singular ('is his favourite'). Correct sentence: 'Bread and butter is his favourite.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0730: The error lies in part (2) 'One of the member'. 'One of the + plural noun' requires 'members'. Correct sentence: 'One of the members is absent.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0731: The error lies in part (1) 'She don't like'. The third-person singular pronoun 'She' takes 'doesn't like', not 'don't like'. Correct sentence: 'She doesn't like sweets.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0732: The error lies in part (2) 'is because'. The expression 'The reason why... is because' is redundant; the correct copular complement is 'is that...'. Correct sentence: 'The reason why he failed is that he was ill.' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0733: The error lies in segment (C) 'A great'. The specific culture of the Spanish people takes the definite article 'The great culture', not 'A great'. Correct sentence: 'The great culture of hospitality of the Spanish is well-known.' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0734: The error lies in segment (D) 'He part the grass'. The narrative is set in the past ('had seen'), requiring the simple past tense 'parted' rather than the base form 'part'. APT-ENG-0735: The error lies in segment (A) 'but returned back'. The verb 'return' already means 'to go or come back'; using 'back' is an erroneous pleonasm. Correct sentence: 'He went to work but returned immediately.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0736: The error lies in segment (D) 'still 10 p.m.'. APT-ENG-0737: The error lies in segment (C) 'good with running'. The idiom for expressing competence or skill in an activity is 'good at' followed by a gerund ('good at running'), not 'good with'. Correct sentence: 'Deepa and Seema are both good at running...' Hence, option C is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0738: Option A provides the correct sentence. The original sentence contained a redundant second auxiliary verb ('Is Savita is joining...'). Option A correctly states: 'Is Savita joining us for lunch today?' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0739: The error lies in segment (A) 'nevertheless my brother does not do'. APT-ENG-0740: The error lies in segment (B) 'same like human beings'. APT-ENG-0741: The error lies in segment (D) 'is led to'. APT-ENG-0742: The error lies in part (2) 'are traveling to the international conference'. Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0743: The error lies in part (2) 'new group of interns'. The singular countable noun phrase 'new group' requires the indefinite article 'a': 'a new group of interns'. Correct sentence: 'The company plans to hire a new group of interns...' Hence, option B is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0744: The error lies in segment (C) 'consequency, we had'. The word 'consequency' is non-standard; the appropriate adverb indicating logical consequence is 'consequently'. APT-ENG-0745: The error lies in part (3) 'have caused significant strain'. APT-ENG-0746: The error lies in segment (B) 'It was a surprising'. APT-ENG-0747: The error lies in segment (A) 'The monkeys swinged'. The simple past tense of the irregular verb 'swing' is 'swung', not 'swinged'. Correct sentence: 'The monkeys swung on the branches and jumped over the compound wall.' Hence, option A is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-0748: The error lies in segment (A) 'which are one of'. APT-ENG-0749: The error lies in part (B) 'A tiger be strayed into a village'. APT-ENG-0750: The error lies in segment (C) 'are allowed'.
